chapters.title: Big Things First
chapters.intro: Every family has one person who can make anything fit. It started with Grandpa Joe, a red wagon, and a picnic.

chapters.title: The Summer of Everything
chapters.intro: Twelve years later, the whole family has your number.

chapters.title: Leaving the Nest
chapters.intro: Dorm rooms, festivals, first apartments. Everything you own, in whatever car you can borrow.

chapters.title: Two of Us
chapters.intro: Someone with six hundred records and a cat needs help moving.

chapters.title: Our Own Front Door
chapters.intro: A house, a nursery, and the most precious cargo you will ever pack.

chapters.title: One More Thing
chapters.intro: Big things first. Fragile on top. And always leave room for one more thing.

items.name: Big Suitcase
items.desc: Dad's. Fourteen outfits for a two-night stay.
items.neighbourDesc: Fourteen outfits for a two-night stay.

items.name: Hard-Shell Suitcase
items.desc: Mom's. Bulletproof. Probably. Please don't test that.
items.neighbourDesc: Bulletproof. Probably. Please don't test that.

items.name: Carry-On
items.desc: Technically within airline size limits.

items.name: Gym Duffel
items.desc: Dad is convinced he'll go jogging. He won't.
items.neighbourDesc: Somebody is convinced they'll go jogging. They won't.

items.name: Backpack
items.desc: Six granola bars, none of them whole.

items.name: Grocery Bag
items.desc: Baguette sold separately.

items.name: Egg Carton
items.desc: Eighteen chances to ruin Grandma's party.
items.neighbourDesc: Eighteen chances to ruin somebody's party.

items.name: Birthday Cake
items.desc: The bakery wrote HAPPY BIRTHDAY GARY. Grandma's name is Rose.
items.neighbourDesc: The bakery wrote HAPPY BIRTHDAY GARY. Nobody here is called Gary.

items.name: 24-Pack of Water
items.desc: Aunt Dee said bring 'some water.'
items.neighbourDesc: Somebody said bring 'some water.'

items.name: Watermelon
items.desc: Heavier than it has any right to be.

items.name: Baguette
items.desc: Structurally load-bearing.

items.name: Bulk Toilet Paper
items.desc: It was on sale. That's the whole story.

items.name: Cereal Box
items.desc: Contains 2% cereal, 98% air.

items.name: Tent Bag
items.desc: Instructions not included. Never were.

items.name: Cooler
items.desc: Ice, sandwiches, and one mysterious fish.

items.name: Sleeping Bag
items.desc: Rated for temperatures you will never camp in.

items.name: Folding Chair
items.desc: Folds in eleven directions, none of them flat.

items.name: Kayak Paddle
items.desc: Always exactly one trunk-length too long.

items.name: Lantern
items.desc: Battery powered. The batteries are in another car.

items.name: Firewood Bundle
items.desc: Bark everywhere. Forever.

items.name: Industrial Marshmallows
items.desc: One bag. Forty pounds.

items.name: Inflatable Flamingo
items.desc: Fully inflated for the lake. The valve is long gone.

items.name: Garden Gnome
items.desc: Dad's lucky gnome. Comes on every trip. Nobody ever voted on this.

items.name: Giant Rubber Duck
items.desc: Wes's Duck Derby entry, Sir Quacksalot. Squeaks when compressed.
items.neighbourDesc: A Duck Derby hopeful. Squeaks when compressed.

items.name: Grandfather Clock
items.desc: Grandpa wound it every Sunday for fifty years. It still chimes every fifteen minutes.

items.name: Grandma's Armchair
items.desc: Grandma's armchair. Smells like lavender and hard candy. Non-negotiable.

items.name: Cat Tree
items.desc: Mr. Whiskers is not coming. The cat tree is.

items.name: Floor Lamp
items.desc: Comes with a pre-installed lampshade dent.

items.name: Potted Ficus
items.desc: Sheds one leaf per pothole.

items.name: Moving Box
items.desc: Labeled MISC. Ominous.

items.name: Box of Cables
items.desc: Every charging cable ever made. None of them fit anything.

items.name: Portrait of Grandpa
items.desc: Grandpa Joe, painted in 1975. His eyes follow you. He'd find that hilarious.

items.name: Lava Lamp
items.desc: From Grandma's hippie days. Extremely fragile. Still groovy.
items.neighbourDesc: From somebody's hippie days. Extremely fragile. Still groovy.

items.name: Disco Ball
items.desc: For emergencies.

items.name: Trombone
items.desc: Slides into any space. Theoretically.

items.name: Tuba
items.desc: For the graduation march. Oompah.

items.name: Unicycle
items.desc: Bonko's graduation project. Previous owner's note: never again.
items.neighbourDesc: Previous owner's note: never again.

items.name: Cream Pies
items.desc: Ammunition.

items.name: Rubber Chicken
items.desc: Screams. Constantly.

items.name: Juggling Pins
items.desc: Not for bowling. Don't ask how we know.

items.name: Size 34 Shoes
items.desc: Size 34. Honk when stepped on.

items.name: Seltzer Bottle
items.desc: Pressurized. Pointed at you.

items.name: A Second Clown
items.desc: Bonko's classmate. Folds. Insists on folding.

items.name: Taxidermy Moose Head
items.desc: Dev's uncle's moose head. It comes to every campfire. Nobody knows why.
items.neighbourDesc: Somebody's uncle's moose head. Nobody knows why it's coming.

items.name: Cardboard Cutout of You
items.desc: Life-size cardboard cutout of you. Grandma's favorite grandkid, apparently.

items.name: Surfboard
items.desc: Uncle Rick's. Wax on. Wax everywhere.
items.neighbourDesc: Wax on. Wax everywhere.

items.name: Kayak
items.desc: Seats one. Fits zero.

items.name: Beach Umbrella
items.desc: Inverts in winds above two miles per hour.

items.name: Boogie Board
items.desc: Rad. Gnarly. Slightly dented.

items.name: Inflatable Shark
items.desc: Uncle Rick named it Bruce.
items.neighbourDesc: Its name is Bruce. Every inflatable shark is called Bruce.

items.name: Tiki Torch
items.desc: A fire hazard, but decorative.

items.name: Kiddie Pool
items.desc: Deflated, yet somehow refuses to fold.

items.name: Bowling Ball
items.desc: Grandma's league ball. She's undefeated since 1987.
items.neighbourDesc: A league ball. Undefeated since 1987, allegedly.

items.name: Kid's Bike
items.desc: Your little cousin's. Training wheels included, dignity not.
items.neighbourDesc: Training wheels included, dignity not.

items.name: Fishing Rod
items.desc: The one that got away was this rod.

items.name: Antique Mirror
items.desc: Antique. Seven years bad luck, minimum.

items.name: The Kitchen Sink
items.desc: Grandma said bring everything but the kitchen sink. Mom heard 'bring the kitchen sink.'
items.neighbourDesc: They said bring everything but the kitchen sink. Somebody misheard.

items.name: Air Mattress
items.desc: Slow leak. Fast attitude.

items.name: Acoustic Guitar
items.desc: Grandpa Joe's guitar. Knows one song. Everyone in the family knows the one.

items.name: Pink Lawn Flamingos
items.desc: A flock of three. They go to every beach party.

items.name: Picnic Basket
items.desc: Grandma's picnic basket. The checkered cloth has seen forty summers.
items.neighbourDesc: The checkered cloth has seen forty summers.

items.name: Birthday Bouquet
items.desc: Ninety roses would not fit. These are nine.

items.name: Last Year's Trophy
items.desc: Duck Derby champion, two years running. Wes polishes it daily.
items.neighbourDesc: Duck Derby champion, two years running. Polished daily.

items.name: Mr. Buttons
items.desc: Grandpa won him at the county fair in 1998. One button eye, one regular eye.

items.name: Wooden Blocks
items.desc: A, B, C, and one that just says JOE. Grandpa carved them.
items.neighbourDesc: A, B, C, and one that's been chewed.

items.name: Lemonade Jug
items.desc: Grandma Rose's recipe. Extra sugar. Don't tell your mom.
items.neighbourDesc: Extra sugar. Nobody has to know.

items.name: Toy Dump Truck
items.desc: Has hauled more sand than most real trucks.

items.name: Grandpa's Note
items.desc: Folded in the wagon since 1998: 'Always leave room for one more thing.'

items.name: Mini Fridge
items.desc: Holds exactly one pizza and forty sodas.

items.name: Desk Lamp
items.desc: Bends toward whatever you're avoiding studying.

items.name: Laundry Hamper
items.desc: Will be used as a chair for four straight years.

items.name: Duck Comforter
items.desc: Mom picked it. It has ducks on it. You are eighteen.
items.neighbourDesc: It has ducks on it. It's not up for discussion.

items.name: Poster Tube
items.desc: Band posters. Mostly bands you'll pretend you never liked.
items.neighbourDesc: Band posters. Mostly bands nobody admits to liking.

items.name: Shower Caddy
items.desc: Seven shampoos. Zero conditioners.

items.name: Party Speaker
items.desc: Goes to eleven. The neighbors go to the police.

items.name: Glow Sticks
items.desc: Two hundred of them. Dev did the math. Dev did not do the math.
items.neighbourDesc: Two hundred of them. Somebody did the math. Badly.

items.name: Futon
items.desc: Couch by day. Bed by night. Back pain always.

items.name: Beanbag
items.desc: Contains about a million foam beads. For now.

items.name: Record Crate
items.desc: Alphabetized. Then by mood. Then by Sam's mood.
items.neighbourDesc: Alphabetized. Then by mood.

items.name: Sam's Turntable
items.desc: Sam's prized turntable. Handle like a baby. Good practice.

items.name: Monstera
items.desc: Sam talks to it every morning. It's doing great.
items.neighbourDesc: Gets talked to every morning. It's doing great.

items.name: Biscuit (in Carrier)
items.desc: Contains Biscuit. Biscuit has opinions about this.

items.name: Toaster
items.desc: One is Sam's. One is yours. You now own two toasters.
items.neighbourDesc: One of two toasters. Nobody knows where the second one came from.

items.name: Sam's Armchair
items.desc: Thrift-store find. Mustard yellow. Also non-negotiable.

items.name: The Ring
items.desc: Do NOT let Sam see this.

items.name: Wedding Cake
items.desc: Three tiers. Two tiny figures on top. Zero room for error.

items.name: Flower Arch
items.desc: Aunt Dee spent two days on it. It is held together with hope.
items.neighbourDesc: Somebody spent two days on it. It is held together with hope.

items.name: Grandma's Veil
items.desc: Rose wore it when she married Joe in 1962. Now it's your turn.

items.name: Champagne Crate
items.desc: Twelve bottles. Uncle Rick has volunteered to 'test' one.
items.neighbourDesc: Twelve bottles. Somebody has volunteered to 'test' one.

items.name: Camera Bag
items.desc: Four hundred photos of sunsets. Six of each other.

items.name: Dad's New Grill
items.desc: His retirement present to himself. It has Bluetooth. Why does it have Bluetooth?

items.name: Tackle Box
items.desc: Forty lures. Dad has caught zero fish with any of them.
items.neighbourDesc: Forty lures. Zero fish caught with any of them.

items.name: Kitchen Table
items.desc: Where every family dinner will happen. And where the mail will pile up.

items.name: Flat-Pack Crib
items.desc: Some assembly required. Some patience also required.

items.name: Rocking Chair
items.desc: Grandma rocked your mom in it. Then you. Now it's Rosie's turn.

items.name: Duck Mobile
items.desc: Little felt ducks. Sir Quacksalot approves.
items.neighbourDesc: Little felt ducks. Very calming, allegedly.

items.name: Diapers (Bulk)
items.desc: Very bulk. You will need more.

items.name: Paint Cans
items.desc: The color is called Morning Duckling. It's yellow.

items.name: Baby Car Seat
items.desc: The most precious cargo you will ever pack.

items.name: Hospital Bag
items.desc: Packed six weeks early. Repacked eleven times.

items.name: IT'S A GIRL Balloons
items.desc: In three colors. Dad bought nine.

items.name: Stroller
items.desc: Folds in one easy motion. The motion is not easy.

items.name: Playpen
items.desc: A tiny fence for a tiny person.

items.name: Duck Bath
items.desc: Duck-shaped. Obviously.

items.name: White Noise Machine
items.desc: Plays the ocean. Rosie prefers the vacuum cleaner setting.
items.neighbourDesc: Plays the ocean. The baby prefers the vacuum cleaner setting.

items.name: Photo Album
items.desc: Ninety years in one book. Bring tissues.

items.name: Grandpa's Sled
items.desc: Still the fastest on the hill. Grandpa made sure of it.

items.name: Skis
items.desc: Two skis, two poles, zero lessons.

items.name: Snowman Kit
items.desc: Carrot, coal buttons, one of Grandpa's old scarves.
items.neighbourDesc: Carrot, coal buttons, one old scarf.

items.name: Cocoa Thermos
items.desc: Hot cocoa. The marshmallows are in the other bag.

items.name: Snow Shovel
items.desc: For the snow. Or for digging out the SUV.

items.name: Costume Trunk
items.desc: Sequins, feathers, a top hat. Grandma's talent show look.
items.neighbourDesc: Sequins, feathers, a top hat. Somebody's talent show look.

items.name: Rosie's Suitcase
items.desc: She packed it herself. One sock, four rocks, and a crayon.

items.name: Toy Box
items.desc: Every toy Rosie owns. She needs all of them. All.
items.neighbourDesc: Every toy they own. They need all of them. All.

items.name: Folding Chairs
items.desc: A stack of six. There will be eleven guests.

items.name: Graduation Balloons
items.desc: CONGRATS in gold. Grandma picked them.
items.neighbourDesc: CONGRATS in gold. Somebody's very proud.

levels.title: The Little Red Wagon
levels.blurb: Grandpa Joe is teaching you to pack. You are seven.
messages: Kiddo! Picnic at the creek today.
The wagon's all yours. You're in charge of packing.
Here's the secret: big things first, fragile on top, and always leave room for one more thing.
epilogues: Grandpa pulled the wagon to the creek and you held Mr. Buttons the whole way.
Grandpa said it was the best-packed wagon in the county. He'd know.
Not a single gap. Grandpa laughed his big laugh and said: 'That's my kid.'

levels.title: Weekend Getaway
levels.blurb: Mom and Dad's anniversary weekend. They 'packed light.'
messages: Your dad and I leave for the lake in 20 minutes.
He packed the car himself. The trunk does not close.
Grandpa always said you were the best packer in the family. HELP
epilogues: They made it to the lake. Dad's jogging duffel stayed in the hallway, where it belongs.
The trunk closed with only a little sitting on it. Happy anniversary!
Everything fit, even the gnome. Mom says you're officially in charge of all future trips.

levels.title: Grocery Run
levels.blurb: Grandma Rose's 80th birthday party. Don't squish the cake.
messages: Grandma's 80th is at 4 and I'm stuck at work!!
Can you grab the groceries and the cake in my hatchback?
The cake says GARY. Don't ask. Don't squish it either.
epilogues: The cake survived. Mostly. Grandma ate the GARY part herself.
Party saved! Grandma wants to know who brought 48 rolls of toilet paper.
Not one egg cracked. Aunt Dee is telling everyone you're a professional.

levels.title: Into the Woods
levels.blurb: Dev bought ALL the camping gear. And borrowed some extra.
messages: CAMPING TRIP! I bought all the gear
Also borrowed your grandpa's guitar, my uncle's moose head, and Wes's duck for 'testing'
The SUV has wheel wells. Why are there always wheel wells
epilogues: You forgot the marshmallows. Dev will never forgive you. Dev is sulking in the tent.
Campfire, guitar, one song on repeat. A perfect night.
Everything came along. The moose watched over the campfire all night.

levels.title: Duck Derby
levels.blurb: Sir Quacksalot is entered in the Duck Derby. The car is a Mini.
messages: Sir Quacksalot is entered in the Duck Derby!!!
Problem: my car is a Mini. Sir Quacksalot is not mini.
Bring the trophy. We're defending the title.
epilogues: Sir Quacksalot made it. The trophy did not. Wes is being brave about it.
Second place! The judges loved the emotional support chicken.
Three-time champion! Not a single spare inch in that trunk. Legendary.

levels.title: Grandma's Big Move
levels.blurb: Grandma is moving into Sunny Pines. She's bringing Grandpa's portrait.
messages: Hello dear, it's Grandma. I'm moving to Sunny Pines on Saturday.
The house has been too quiet since your grandpa passed.
I'm bringing the essentials. And Joe's portrait. He'd hate being left behind.
epilogues: Grandma arrived with most of it. The cardboard you is staying with the neighbors.
Joe's portrait went up first. Grandma says the room feels right now.
Every single thing made it. Grandma hung the portrait, wound the clock, and cried a little. The good kind.

levels.title: Surf's Up
levels.blurb: Uncle Rick's beach day. A long, beautiful truck bed. Ruined by a toolbox.
messages: Duuude. Beach day at Gull Point
Two boards, the kayak, Bruce the shark, the whole crew
Toolbox is welded in. Long story. Work around it
epilogues: Uncle Rick paddled out with what fit. The lawn flamingos watched from the driveway.
Gnarly day. Bruce the shark scared three seagulls.
The whole crew made it to the beach. Uncle Rick called you 'the GOAT of trunks.'

levels.title: The Clown Car
levels.blurb: Bonko graduates from clown college today. Someone is already in the car.
messages: I GRADUATE TODAY
Need my tuba, trombone, pies, chickens, and unicycle at the ceremony
Heads up: there's already a clown in the car. He lives there now
epilogues: Bonko graduated with honks. One seltzer bottle was left behind, which is probably for the best.
The march was a triumph. Several pies were deployed.
Every prop, every pie. Bonko's speech thanked you before the faculty.

levels.title: Everything But...
levels.blurb: The whole family is driving to see Grandma. Everyone's bringing everything.
messages: Family reunion at Sunny Pines this weekend!
Everyone is bringing everything. Dev is bringing the moose.
Grandma said 'bring everything but the kitchen sink.' Your dad heard that wrong.
epilogues: Most of the family's stuff made it. The kitchen sink is waiting by the curb, hopeful.
The whole family made it to Sunny Pines. Grandma made lemonade.
The minivan held a whole summer. The kitchen sink is now in Grandma's garden. Packing Legend.

levels.title: Dorm Bound
levels.blurb: Your first dorm room. Mom insists on driving.
messages: I can't believe my baby is going to college.
I put Mr. Buttons in the bag. You said you didn't want him. He's in the bag.
Aunt Dee's hatchback again. You know what to do.
epilogues: Most of it made it. Mr. Buttons rode home with Mom. She says he'll keep your room warm.
You moved in before lunch. Mom cried in the parking lot. Twice.
Your roommate asked how you fit all that in a hatchback. You said: big things first.

levels.title: Festival Weekend
levels.blurb: Dev's mom's minivan, three days of music, and too many glow sticks.
messages: THREE DAYS. FOUR BANDS I'VE HEARD OF.
I borrowed my mom's minivan. And two tents. And a flamingo.
Grandma let me borrow your grandpa's guitar. I promised to be careful.
epilogues: You got there. The flamingo did not. Dev has written it a eulogy.
Three days of mud and music. Dev learned the one song on Grandpa's guitar.
Everything fit, even the beanbag. Dev's mom says you can borrow the van anytime.

levels.title: Move-Out Day
levels.blurb: Uncle Rick's truck. Two years of dorm life. One futon.
messages: Duuude. Heard you need a truck.
The toolbox is still welded in. Still a long story.
Grandma says her lava lamp better survive your dorm years. No pressure.
epilogues: The futon made it. The ficus did not. It had a good run.
Two years of dorm life in one truck bed. Uncle Rick is impressed. Quietly.
Grandma's lava lamp survived. She's telling everyone at Sunny Pines.

levels.title: The Big City
levels.blurb: Your first apartment. Wes's Mini. Everything you own.
messages: You got the job!! First apartment in the city!
My Mini is the only car I have. Sir Quacksalot is NOT coming. Probably.
Grandma sent a cutting from her ficus. She says every home needs something growing.
epilogues: Your first apartment is tiny and perfect. The ficus cutting is on the windowsill.
Wes helped you carry everything up five flights. Sir Quacksalot supervised.
Every inch used. Mom mailed Mr. Buttons with a note: 'For the new place.'

levels.title: Cap and Gown
levels.blurb: Graduation party. Grandma insists Grandpa comes too.
messages: Hello dear. I'm so proud of you I could burst.
Dee is driving us to the party. She drives just like your grandpa did.
Bring Joe's portrait, would you? He should see this.
epilogues: The party was lovely. Grandpa's portrait had the best seat.
Grandma gave a speech. Nobody had a dry eye. Not even Uncle Rick.
Grandpa's portrait watched you cross the stage. The cake said CONGRATULATIONS GARY.

levels.title: Six Hundred Records
levels.blurb: Sam has six hundred records and a cat. You have a hatchback.
messages: Hi! Dev says you're the person to call about packing?
I have six hundred records, one turntable, a monstera, and a cat named Biscuit.
Biscuit has opinions. Please don't take them personally.
epilogues: Most of it made it. Sam made you dinner as a thank-you. You stayed till midnight.
Biscuit sat on your lap the whole drive. Sam says that has never happened before.
Every record, every leaf. Sam asked if you're free next Saturday. Not for packing.

levels.title: Two of Everything
levels.blurb: Merging two lives into one station wagon. Two toasters included.
messages: Big day! Our first place together.
Grandma lent us her station wagon. She says it's lucky.
We own two toasters now. We are keeping both. This is non-negotiable.
epilogues: Home, mostly. One toaster stayed behind. Sam is grieving.
Sam put your ficus next to the monstera. They seem happy.
Two lives, one wagon. Biscuit claimed the armchair within four minutes.

levels.title: The Question
levels.blurb: A camping trip. Sam doesn't know about the ring.
messages: Okay. I've got the SUV. Sam thinks it's just a camping trip.
Grandma gave me Grandpa's guitar for you. She said 'tell them to play the song.'
The ring is in the little red box. DO NOT pack it under anything.
epilogues: Sam said yes before you finished the song. The marshmallows were forgotten. Nobody cared.
You played the one song by the fire. Sam said yes. Dev cried the hardest.
Everything perfect. Sam said yes. Grandma answered the phone on the first ring.

levels.title: Wedding Day
levels.blurb: The wedding is in Grandma's garden. The cake has three tiers.
levels.trip: June · The Garden at Sunny Pines
messages: The wedding is at Sunny Pines!! Grandma insisted.
The cake is three tiers. If it falls over I will simply walk into the sea.
Grandma's veil is in the white box. She wore it when she married your grandpa.
epilogues: Married! Bonko's juggling pins stayed home. Probably for the best.
Grandma watched you walk down the aisle in her veil. She held Joe's photo the whole time.
Not one crumb out of place. Grandma danced with Dad. Dad cried. Dad always cries.

levels.title: Just Married
levels.blurb: Uncle Rick's convertible. Pack light. Leave room for souvenirs.
messages: Honeymoon road trip!! Uncle Rick lent us his convertible.
He said 'treat her like family.' He meant the car.
Pack light. Leave room for souvenirs.
epilogues: Just married, a little cramped. The beach umbrella rode in Sam's lap.
Coast road, top down, Biscuit at the neighbors'. Perfect.
Perfectly packed. Sam says it's the most romantic trunk they've ever seen.

levels.title: Gone Fishing
levels.blurb: Dad is retiring. The gnome is retiring with him.
messages: It's your dad. I'm retired! I'm going fishing every day.
I bought a grill. It has Bluetooth. I don't know why.
Bringing the gnome. He's retiring too. He's earned it.
epilogues: Dad caught nothing. Dad was delighted anyway.
Dad grilled with Bluetooth. Nobody knows what the Bluetooth does.
Everything packed, gnome included. Dad sent a photo of him and the gnome at sunrise.

levels.title: Our Own Front Door
levels.blurb: A house of your own. Grandma's armchair is coming with you.
messages: WE BOUGHT A HOUSE.
Grandma says her armchair should go to us. She says it's time.
Rented the big truck. Biscuit is furious about everything.
epilogues: Home. A few boxes stayed at the old place. You'll go back for them. Probably.
Grandma's armchair is by the window. Biscuit has already claimed it.
Every last thing. You stood in the empty living room, then it wasn't empty anymore.

levels.title: Grandma's 90th
levels.blurb: Ten years later. Same hatchback. Same bakery.
messages: Grandma turns NINETY on Sunday!!
Same hatchback. Same bakery. Guess what the cake says.
It says GARY. They remembered. Grandma is thrilled.
epilogues: The cake survived. Grandma ate the GARY part herself. Again.
Ninety candles. The fire department was very understanding.
Grandma read the photo album out loud, every page. Then she said: 'Now, where's my lemonade?'

levels.title: Flat-Pack Nursery
levels.blurb: Grandma's rocking chair and an 84-piece crib.
messages: So. The nursery.
Grandma's sending over the rocking chair. She rocked your mom in it. And you.
The crib has 84 pieces. I have counted them three times.
epilogues: The crib has 83 pieces now. It's fine. It's sturdy. Mostly.
The nursery is Morning Duckling yellow. The mobile spins all on its own.
Everything built and ready. You sat in Grandma's rocking chair and practiced humming.

levels.title: Coming Home
levels.blurb: Bringing Rosie home. Drive slow.
messages: She's perfect. Grandma cried. Your dad cried more.
Rosie. You named her after Grandma. Grandma hasn't stopped smiling.
Grandma found Mr. Buttons in her attic. She says he's Rosie's now.
epilogues: Rosie slept the whole way home. You checked on her eleven times.
Home. Mr. Buttons is guarding the crib. He takes it very seriously.
The most precious cargo you'll ever pack, packed perfectly. Welcome home, Rosie.

levels.title: Everything a Baby Needs
levels.blurb: Rosie weighs 18 pounds. Her stuff weighs 400.
messages: First family vacation! Three days at the beach.
Rosie weighs 18 pounds. Her stuff weighs 400.
Uncle Rick says the kiddie pool is a 'must.' Uncle Rick doesn't have to pack it.
epilogues: The kiddie pool stayed home. Rosie played in the sand instead. She ate some.
Rosie's first beach. She laughed at every single wave.
Everything a baby needs, and then some. Rosie fell asleep under the umbrella with Mr. Buttons.

levels.title: First Snow
levels.blurb: Rosie's first snow. Grandpa's sled is still the fastest.
messages: It SNOWED at the cabin! Bring Rosie!
Grandma says Grandpa's old sled is in her garage. Bring that too.
I have the cocoa. You bring everything else. As usual.
epilogues: Rosie rode Grandpa's sled down the bunny hill. Then fifty more times.
A snowman with one of Grandpa's old scarves. Grandma made you send three photos.
Every last thing. Snowman, sled, cocoa by the fire. Rosie's first snow was perfect.

levels.title: The Sunny Pines Talent Show
levels.blurb: Grandma's talent show act is a secret. It involves a tuba.
messages: GRANDMA SIGNED UP FOR THE TALENT SHOW.
Her act is a secret. She needs a tuba, a disco ball, and Grandpa's guitar.
The other clown is still in the car. He's her backup dancer now.
epilogues: Grandma won second place. First place went to a man who whistled. She's demanding a recount.
Grandma played the one song on Grandpa's guitar. The whole room sang along.
Grandma won first prize. She dedicated it to Joe, then made the clown take a bow.

levels.title: Little Helper
levels.blurb: Rosie is packing for her first sleepover. She needs help.
messages: Rosie has insisted on packing her own bag for Grandma's.
She packed one sock and four rocks.
She says you have to help, because you're the best packer in the whole world.
epilogues: Rosie forgot her toothbrush, but brought the rocks. Grandma says that's the important stuff.
Rosie packed Mr. Buttons first. 'Big things first,' she said. You didn't teach her that.
Every gap filled. Rosie high-fived you. Grandma says she's a natural.

levels.title: Coming Home to Us
levels.blurb: Grandma's moving in. She's bringing Grandpa.
messages: Hello dear. Sunny Pines has been lovely.
But I'd rather spend my mornings with Rosie. If you'll have me.
I'm only bringing the essentials. The clock. And Joe, of course.
epilogues: Grandma moved in. Rosie gave her a tour of every room. Twice.
The clock is in the hallway. It chimes every fifteen minutes. Rosie counts along.
Everything came home. Grandma hung Joe's portrait next to your wedding photo. 'There,' she said.

levels.title: Lake Mirabel, Again
levels.blurb: Mom and Dad's 40th anniversary. Back to the lake, all of us.
messages: Forty years married! We're going back to the lake. All of us.
Your dad packed the car himself. The trunk does not close.
Some things never change.
epilogues: Three generations at the lake. Dad's jogging duffel stayed home. Again.
Dad brought the gnome. Rosie brought the flamingo. Grandma brought the lemonade.
Everything fit. Mom said: 'Just like the first time.' Dad cried. Dad always cries.

levels.title: The Garage Sale
levels.blurb: Everything must go. Except the things that mustn't.
messages: Garage sale this weekend! Everything must go.
Except the gnome. And Grandma's lava lamp. And the duck comforter, apparently.
We still own two toasters. One of them has to go. You choose.
epilogues: Half of it sold. The duck comforter came back home. Nobody's surprised.
The futon went to a college kid. You told them: big things first.
Garage cleared. Grandma bought the lava lamp back for a dollar.

levels.title: Everyone, Everything
levels.blurb: The whole family. Every last thing.
messages: Family reunion at the lake! Everybody's coming!
Dev's bringing the moose. Wes is bringing Sir Quacksalot. Bonko is bringing a second clown.
And yeah. The kitchen sink. Grandma's orders.
epilogues: Everyone made it. Most of everything made it. That counts.
Thirty people, one lake, one song on Grandpa's guitar.
Everyone, everything. Grandma looked around the campfire and said: 'Joe would've loved this.'

levels.title: One More Thing
levels.blurb: Grandpa's wagon, a picnic at the creek, and Rosie.
messages: I found Joe's old wagon in the attic. A little paint and it's good as new.
Rosie wants a picnic at the creek. Just like you used to.
I think it's your turn to teach her. Joe would love that.
epilogues: Rosie pulled the wagon all by herself. Mostly.
You told Rosie the secret: big things first, fragile on top.
Rosie found the note tucked in the wagon. 'Always leave room for one more thing.' She asked what it meant. You looked at your family, and you told her.
